question: Which organization regulates nursing education in India?
explanation: • Indian Nursing Council (INC) is the statutory body that regulates nursing education and practice in India, established under the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947.

question: What is the theme of International Nurses Day 2024?
options: A. Nurses: A Voice to Lead
C. Nursing the World to Health
D. A Vision for Future Healthcare
explanation: • International Nurses Day 2024 theme is 'Our Nurses, Our Future' focusing on investing in nursing to transform healthcare.

question: Which program provides health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh per family?
options: D. Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
explanation: • Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) provides health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year for hospitalization.

question: What is the full form of WHO?
explanation: • WHO stands for World Health Organization, a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health.

question: Which year was declared as the International Year of the Nurse and Midwife?
explanation: • 2020 was declared the International Year of the Nurse and Midwife by WHO to recognize their crucial role in healthcare, coinciding with Florence Nightingale's 200th birth anniversary.

question: What is the minimum qualification for Nursing Officer in AIIMS?
explanation:
• B.Sc.
• Nursing (4 years) or Post Basic B.Sc.
• Nursing is the minimum qualification for Nursing Officer position in AIIMS through NORCET.

question: Which disease was declared eradicated from India in 2014?
explanation:
• India was declared polio-free by WHO in 2014 after the last case was reported in 2011.
• This was achieved through intensive immunization campaigns.

question: What is the target year for eliminating TB from India?
explanation:
• India aims to eliminate TB by 2025, five years ahead of the global SDG target of 2030.
• The National Strategic Plan focuses on early detection and treatment.

question: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
explanation: • Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness (nyctalopia) and can lead to xerophthalmia and permanent blindness if untreated.

question: What is the full form of ASHA?
explanation: • ASHA stands for Accredited Social Health Activist, community health workers who act as link between community and health system under NHM.

question: Which organization conducts NORCET exam?
explanation: • NORCET (Nursing Officer Recruitment Common Entrance Test) is conducted by AIIMS, New Delhi for recruitment of Nursing Officers in various AIIMS institutions.

question: What is the recommended daily water intake for adults?
explanation: • Recommended daily water intake is 2-3 liters (8-10 glasses) for adults, varying with activity level, climate, and health status.

question: Which program focuses on reducing maternal and infant mortality?
options: C. Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana
explanation:

question: What is the normal body temperature in Celsius?
explanation:
• Normal body temperature ranges from 36.5-37.5°C (97.7-99.5°F).
• Temperature varies with age, time of day, and activity level.

question: Which day is observed as World Health Day?
explanation:
• World Health Day is observed on April 7 every year to mark the founding of WHO in 1948.
• Each year has a specific health theme.

question: What is the full form of NHM?
explanation: • NHM stands for National Health Mission, which includes National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and National Urban Health Mission (NUHM) to provide universal health coverage.

question: Which vitamin is synthesized by the body on exposure to sunlight?
explanation:
• Vitamin D is synthesized in the skin when exposed to UVB sunlight.
• It's essential for calcium absorption and bone health.

question: What is the target for reducing MMR (Maternal Mortality Ratio) in India?
explanation:
• India aims to reduce MMR to less than 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030 as per SDG targets.
• Current MMR is around 97.

question: Which disease is prevented by BCG vaccine?
explanation: • BCG (Bacille Calmette-Guérin) vaccine prevents tuberculosis, especially severe forms like TB meningitis and miliary TB in children.

question: What is the recommended age for retirement of nurses in government hospitals?
explanation:
• Retirement age for nurses in government hospitals is typically 60 years, though this may vary by state and institution policies.

question: Which program provides free medicines and diagnostics in public health facilities?
options: C. Free Medicine and Diagnostic Service
explanation: • Free Drug Service and Free Diagnostic Service initiatives provide essential medicines and diagnostic tests free of cost in public health facilities under NHM.

question: What is the full form of DOTS?
explanation: • DOTS stands for Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course, the WHO-recommended strategy for TB control ensuring patients take medications as prescribed.

question: Which organization sets standards for nursing practice globally?
explanation: • ICN (International Council of Nurses) is the global voice for nursing, setting standards and promoting excellence in nursing practice worldwide.

question: What is the recommended frequency for hand hygiene in healthcare settings?
options: C. Before and after patient contact
D. Only when hands are visibly dirty
explanation: • WHO's 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene include: before patient contact, before aseptic procedure, after body fluid exposure, after patient contact, and after contact with patient surroundings.

question: What is the full form of PACS in healthcare?
options: B. Picture Archiving and Communication System
explanation:
• PACS stands for Picture Archiving and Communication System - used for storing, retrieving, and distributing medical images (X-rays, CT scans, MRIs) digitally.
• This technology improves efficiency and enables remote access to images.
• Understanding healthcare IT systems is essential for modern nursing practice.

question: What is the full form of HMIS in healthcare?
explanation:
• HMIS stands for Health Management Information System - used for collecting, processing, and using health information for decision-making.
• Essential for healthcare planning and monitoring.
• Understanding healthcare information systems is important for nursing administration and public health.
